decision: Treat issue #2 as the step 6 'Aliases' contract work rather than a corruption bug, because on current main any file with an anchor already exits 4
reason: Running the reporter's file on main gives exit 4 'anchor not supported' and leaves the file untouched, so the corruption described cannot happen

decision: Proceed with one new spec, config-aliases, plus step-6 notes in config-foundation and config-set-writeback, without stopping to ask the owner
reason: The instructions said to proceed, so the arm chose the path itself; it is easy to change

decision: Loader expands aliases into the tree, and every node reached through an alias records that alias (AliasRef provenance), so readers need no change
options: Keep aliases as a separate node kind that each reader resolves
reason: Follows the step 5 pattern; readers would drift apart with per-reader resolution; expanding without provenance is the reported bug; a parser rewrite is unnecessary

decision: Render the expanded copy with the project's own emitter, not by re-dumping with ruamel
options: Re-dump the anchored subtree with ruamel
reason: ruamel decides quoting, widths and float forms, which breaks the byte-surgical contract

decision: Do not write the expansion as `<<: *d` plus an override key
reason: Forbidden by the contract: merge keys are never written

decision: Scope out creating new anchors or aliases from VALUE, renaming or removing anchors, expanding every alias at once, Windows, and concurrent writers
Reuse the existing brief directory as the feature name config-aliases
reason: Discovery had already created it with only brief.md, and the name matches the contract section 'Aliases'

decision: Choice 1: merge keys load (Requirement 2), which departs from the brief's default of keeping exit 4
options: Keep exit 4 for merge keys (the brief's proposal)
reason: The contract names merge keys, so files with them are in contract, and loading cannot change a byte; writes through them are still refused

decision: Choice 2: a PATH that names the alias's own key counts as reached through the alias and exits 3 unless --expand-alias is given
reason: The literal reading is safer, and --expand-alias covers the need

decision: Choice 3: when PATH passes through several aliases, --expand-alias expands each one, outermost first, each with its own comment
options: Expand only the first and refuse the rest
reason: Otherwise the command could never succeed

decision: Choice 4: a copy never repeats inner anchors, and inner aliases are copied as aliases
reason: Copying anchors redefines names and silently changes later aliases; expanding inner aliases changes more than was asked

decision: Choice 5: for a `- *d` list item the comment goes on the item's line, and an alias inside a flow collection is refused with exit 3
reason: A block copy cannot be written inside flow style

decision: Choice 6: when the key's line already has an end-of-line comment, --expand-alias is refused with exit 3
reason: Both alternatives lose or alter the user's text

decision: Choice 7: the copy holds values only, in block style at the file's indentation, keeps source styles, and does not copy comments
Choice 8: when an anchored node is replaced, the anchor stays on the new value
reason: The contract says the change is made at the anchor

decision: Choice 9: --expand-alias with no alias on PATH is accepted, and the set runs as without it
reason: Same as the --in-include choice 3

decision: Choice 10: --expand-alias with a VALUE equal to the current value still expands and records no event
reason: Expanding is what was asked, and no leaf value changes

decision: Choice 11: a collection replacement that would change values reached through aliases below PATH is refused, or expanded with the flag
Choice 12: removing an anchored node that a later alias still uses is refused with exit 3
reason: The file would no longer load

decision: Choice 13: anchors on includes load, and converting an anchored scalar-form include to mapping form is refused with exit 3
reason: No written rule says where the anchor goes during the conversion

decision: Choice 14: --sources labels a value reached through an alias with the file of its anchored node
reason: Aliases are local to one file

decision: Choice 15: undefined aliases, recursive aliases, anchors on keys, aliases as keys, bad merge values and a merge key in $ref overrides exit 4 on load; a reused anchor name is accepted as YAML specifies
reason: YAML specifies that each alias refers to the most recent definition

decision: Choice 16: merged keys take the place of the `<<` entry, in the order of the merged mappings
Choice 17: a no-op set through an alias is still refused with exit 3
reason: The contract's rule has no exception for no-op sets, and the user learns about the sharing either way; this fixed a contradiction found in the review gate

decision: Merge keys whose value is not a mapping or a list of mappings, a merge key in mapping-form include overrides, and a quoted `<<` (an ordinary key) are handled as stated in Requirement 2.3/2.4
Design Decision 1: record alias occurrences with a composer subclass that overrides compose_node(parent, index)
options: Match the n-th revisit by id(node) to AliasEvents from a second parse
reason: Exact and independent of visiting order; the other options are order-dependent or fragile

decision: Decision 2: alias places are rebuilt nodes that carry the anchored node's origins, so writes replicate through the step 5 with_other_places machinery
reason: Readers see per-path nodes; written locations are shared, so a write at the anchor replicates

decision: Decision 3: an anchored node's span excludes its &name property, and the layout treats the property as part of the indicator
options: Keep the span at & and teach every edit path to skip the property
reason: Every existing replacement then keeps &name without per-rule changes

decision: Decision 4: merge keys become a merged view, with the written mapping kept (MergeKey) and merged entries marked via_merge, in a new merge_keys.py
reason: Same shape as step 5's include.form; a merge key inside $ref overrides is refused rather than combining two mechanisms

decision: Decision 5: one guard (alias_sites) decides refuse, expand or proceed before planning and before the no-op check
reason: One place for 'reached through an alias'; running before the no-op check keeps 5.3 and 8.6

decision: The guard keeps conservative leftovers on purpose: a new key below an include whose $ref is an alias is refused, whole-subtree changes count on every side, and a deep-merged entry keeps via_merge
reason: The guard does not decide where new content is written

decision: Decision 6: expand in memory, reload, and repeat; then run the unchanged set pipeline, with one atomic write and verification against the original document
options: Plan the expansion edits and the set edits in one _Planner
reason: The edits overlap and apply_edits refuses that; positions inside the copy do not exist in the loaded document

decision: Decision 7: add a new copy renderer over the written anchored node instead of reusing render_yaml or render_block_value
reason: render_yaml loses quoting and line endings and is in the CLI layer; NewValue cannot hold aliases or includes as written

decision: Decision 8: removing a used anchor and converting an anchored include are refused explicitly in the planner
reason: The read-back would also fail, but with a message that does not name the anchor

decision: The 4.7 refusal fires whenever an include root carries an anchor, including chains converted at an inner include (stricter than needed)
reason: Conservative: nothing is written; revisit if users need overrides below anchored include chains

decision: --expand-alias on an anchored node that holds `<<` is refused with the merge-key message plus the alias name
reason: The copy would have to write `<<` (9.1)

decision: Add no limit on exponential alias expansion (billion laughs)
reason: Configurations are small, local and hand-edited, and no limit is in the contract; revisit for untrusted sources

decision: Keep ruamel pinned at 0.19.1 and rely on its non-public compose_node signature, with tests that pin the recorded spans
reason: The composer hook depends on it

decision: Silence ReusedAnchorWarning narrowly around composing
reason: A reused name is valid YAML, and the warning would reach stderr

decision: Design clarification: overrides.deep_merge keeps the anchor, alias and merge fields from the included side
reason: Otherwise an alias behind $ref overrides would lose its marker and the guard would miss it

decision: Refusal order: target resolution first, then the alias guard, then planner refusals
The widened intended configuration comes from the expanded document, while verification runs against the original files
Stop task-plan generation after the second sanity review returned NEEDS_FIXES, and ask for approval of the design clarifications before committing
reason: The skill allows only one repair round, and the design was already approved

decision: Add a temporary set refusal (exit 3) for any configuration with an anchor, alias or merge key between tasks 2.1 and 4.1
reason: So that no intermediate commit can write through an alias

decision: In task 2.1, refuse aliases on load (exit 4, 'not supported yet') until task 2.2 builds alias places
reason: Keeps an alias from silently loading as a plain copy

decision: Put every test for this spec in a fixed list of new files, and limit the traceability check to those files
reason: Earlier specs use the same Req N.M numbers

decision: Remove (P) from task 3.4 and make 3.6 depend on 3.3
reason: 3.4 depends on 3.1; 3.6 needs AliasSite from 3.3

decision: Run implementation autonomously, with a fresh implementer, an independent reviewer and a commit for each sub-task
Give MERGE_KEY a single home in config/constants.py, imported by the loader and yaml_style
reason: structure.md: 'one decision, one place'

decision: Where several aliases are used as keys in one mapping, record only the first
reason: That is enough for the alias-as-key refusal

decision: Detect tags next to anchors by a token scan (_tags_next_to_anchors); an anchor on an include is recorded with its span in the including file
reason: ruamel starts an anchored node's marks at the anchor

decision: Alias-place roots also carry the anchor field, and every consumer must check alias before anchor; accept `$ref: *i`
reason: An alias place is a full rebuild

decision: Refuse includes as merge sources (exit 4), refuse `<<: *list`, and let `<<: []` merge nothing
A merged entry reused by deep_merge keeps via_merge, so the guard treats it as reached through a merge key
reason: Conservative

decision: FileLayout.entry_slot raises ValueError for via_merge entries; callers must refuse or resolve to own entries first
The merge-key precedence rule lives only in merge_keys.merged_pairs, shared by merge_mapping and _Rebuild
The planner keeps its own backstop refusal for any PATH through a merged entry; a whole replacement of a mapping with `<<` is refused; new keys take the style of the last own entry
reason: A backstop behind the guard

decision: _entry_bounds removes an anchored list item together with its &name
Expander refusals name site.path, and the setter re-raises them with the user's PATH; expand.py may import writeback.value (one dependency beyond the design)
reason: expand_alias has no PATH

decision: An anchored empty null expands to `key:  # expanded from *d by troupe`, and a full-line comment between a key and an alias on the next line is refused
reason: So the comment is never lost

decision: At the end of a file without a final line break, the copy adds no final break unless its last line ends a clip or keep block scalar
reason: config-set-writeback 11.6

decision: In the explicit-key test, pin the indentation step with an earlier nested mapping instead of changing the layout's step detection
reason: The column-4 step comes from existing layout behaviour after `? `, which is outside this spec

decision: Add task 3.8 during implementation: replicate a replacement of an anchored node itself to its alias places (WrittenChanges.anchored)
reason: Review of 3.5 found that read-back refused a correct write

decision: Keep one space before the comment after `&d 5`
reason: config-set-writeback 12.2

decision: Add task 3.9: an anchored block list item replaced by a mapping keeps `- &d` alone on its line, with the mapping below (has_property)
reason: YAML reads the compact form's anchor as belonging to the key, so read-back refused it

decision: Also fix a flow item replaced by a mapping and a mapping item replaced by a list in task 3.9
Guard: treat a change of collection kind as removing every child (_same_kind)
reason: Fixes a guard crash when a mapping is replaced by a list

decision: After each expansion round, refuse (exit 3, EXPANSION_CHANGES_VALUES) if the configuration changed, and refuse a stuck expansion (EXPANSION_STUCK) instead of raising RuntimeError
options: Reviewer's wording naming the inner alias (*e)
reason: Safety net for a copied inner alias that binds to a redefined anchor; the message names the expanded alias because the setter cannot tell which inner alias rebound

decision: Replace the closure in _expanded with a module-level helper, _alias_refusal
After expanding an empty mapping alias, setting a key in it gives `s: {k: 1} # expanded...` with one space before the comment
reason: 7.7 applies the usual comment rules (config-set-writeback 12.2); confirmed by the reviewer

decision: Implement --expand-alias as an argparse store_true flag, so `--expand-alias=TEXT` is argparse's usage error (exit 2)
reason: Same rules as --in-include

decision: Check each recorded alias span against the source text, and treat a mismatch as an internal load error
reason: Guards against changes to the ruamel internal hook

decision: Update earlier specs only by adding step-6 notes (never rewriting earlier text) and mark decision H as superseded
Update the loader docstring to describe decision H as narrowed by config-aliases
Commit on main without pushing
